note: Numbers transcribed from explicitly identified primary-source tables or abstracts; no digitization. These are heterogeneous operators, not samples of one common sky map.

records.selection: Selected Loop I spur pixels at l=40–0 deg, b=18–78 deg, plus l=360–327 deg, b=67–78 deg; temperatures 38000–70000 K before background subtraction
records.operator: mean of selected spur pixels minus mean of nearby outer-side pixels below lower contour; 22 MHz survey beam about 1.1 x 1.7 deg
records.independence: potential_partial_holdout; source 22 MHz map not explicitly used as shell-specific calibration in inspected pipeline
records.caveat: One Loop I number, not independent S1/S2 values; contour-based foreground/background choice and gradients can bias excess.

records.selection: l=57–30 deg,b=-50–-10 deg plus l=195–130 deg,b=-70–-2 deg; contour range 30500–80000 K
records.caveat: Selected spur-area excess, not full loop or pixel brightness.
Selected spur-area excess, not full loop or pixel brightness.

records.selection: l=325–285 deg,b=55–72 deg; contour range 36000–46000 K
records.caveat: This high-latitude total-intensity section differs from the Loop IV polarized IVA region of Panopoulou 2021.

records.operator: Gaia stellar distances at transition to optical-starlight/radio-synchrotron polarization-angle alignment
records.independence: partial; radio polarization is independent of modeled total-intensity amplitudes, but object association is assumed
records.caveat: Sightline-associated polarized structure distance, not S1/S2 shell center distance or full radio spur distance.
Published as ≤105 pc; not a Gaussian point estimate.
Sightline-associated polarized structure distance, not shell center.
Paper reports evidence of chance superposition in Loop IV. This region is distinct from Borka's b=55–72 deg Loop IV area.

records.operator: peak extinction surface extracted from Edenhofer et al. 3D dust map
records.independence: prior_reuse; repository conditioning directly cites this result
records.caveat: Dust surface, not ionized wall or radio emissivity boundary. Published surface span 70 to >600 pc; typical dust-traced thickness 35 pc.

fitted_spectral_indices_not_independent_.caveat: Uses the same 22 MHz measurements plus published higher-frequency loop averages. Paper warns these slopes are affected by the 22 MHz point; intermediate frequencies needed to identify turnover.
